newsitem.title: USA: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.
newsitem.headline: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.

text.p: Boxed beef trading was steady to firm on fairly light demand and light to moderate offerings, USDA said.

Retail demand was for immediate fill in needs, while forward interest was rather light early in the trading period. Increased export demand helped stimulate Choice chuck cuts higher, while their Select counterparts traded higher to start the week, but lost some of their early week gains by the end of the trading period.
Round cuts traded higher as these cuts did see fairly good demand for immediate ship.

Choice rib and loin cuts traded higher, while Select rib and loin cuts traded mostly steady after last weeks big increases. Closely trimmed items traded steady to firm with the Choice chuck and round cuts experiencing notable increases. Beef trimmings traded higher early in the week on a light test, but by mid to late week, they were trading at slightly lower levels on mostly moderate demand and offerings.
Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items were generally steady on light to moderate demand and offerings. However, the 73% fed cattle grinds were trading higher late in the week.

For the week - Select and Choice rib primal 1.00 to 2.50 higher; Select and Choice chuck primal steady to 2.00 higher; Select and Choice round primal 1.00 higher; Select and Choice loin primal steady to 2.00 higher; Closely trimmed items steady to 1.00 higher; Beef trimmings 1.00 lower; Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items generally steady.

The Estimated Composite of Boxed Beef Cutout values of Choice 1-3 550/700 carcasses Up 1.31 at 102.76; 700/850 Up 1.65 at 103.27; Select 1-3 550/700 carcasses Up .06 at 97.75; 700/850 Up .25 at 97.34.

COW and BULL CARCASS, BONELESS PROCESSING BEEF, CUTTER COW CUTOUT The lean boneless beef market rebounded after last week's losses as offerings were light and demand was moderate. In addition, the lower lean percentage boneless beef items continued to trade higher on moderate demand and offerings.

Because of the strength in the boneless beef market, coupled with higher live prices, the cow carcass market traded steady to firm on moderate demand and light to moderate offerings. The cow cuts were unevenly steady with the 100% lean supermill, along with the 100% lean flats and eyes, weakened. In addition, the majority of the other cuts traded firm on light offerings and light to moderate demand.
Utility steady to 1.00 higher and Cutter carcasses not established; 90% boneless beef 5.00-7.00 higher; 85% 3.00-3.50 higher; 75% steady to 2.00 higher; 65% 2.00 higher.
The Cutter cow carcass gross cut-out value for Thursday, July 24, 1997 was estimated at 82.15 per cwt., up 3.72 from a week ago Friday.
